props.title: Salt
props.initialSlug: CIA agent fights to clear her name of treason

sections.content: Salt (2010) revolutionized female-led action films by subverting expectations at every turn. Originally written for Tom Cruise, the role of CIA agent Evelyn Salt was reworked for Angelina Jolie without changing the character's intensity or physical demands. This followed Jolie's action credentials established in Tomb Raider (2001) and Wanted (2008), but Salt pushed further into Jason Bourne territory with its complex espionage plot and brutal hand-to-hand combat sequences. The film's paranoid Cold War throwback atmosphere draws from classics like The Manchurian Candidate (1962) while updating the spy thriller for modern audiences.

sections.content: The film's influence can be seen in subsequent female-led action thrillers like Atomic Blonde (2017) and Black Widow (2021). Director Phillip Noyce, who previously helmed Clear and Present Danger (1994) and Patriot Games (1992), brings a veteran's understanding of how to craft sophisticated political thrillers. The film's practical stunts and effects ground the action in reality, while the twisting narrative keeps viewers guessing about Salt's true loyalties until the very end.

The film's exploration of sleeper agents and deep cover operatives taps into post-Cold War anxieties that remain relevant today. Like Bridge of Spies (2015) and Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy (2011), Salt examines how espionage shapes identity and loyalty. The movie's action sequences, particularly the church siege and highway chase, influenced later films like Fast & Furious 6 (2013) in their ambitious scope and practical execution. SUBHEAD: Evolution of the Female Action Hero

movies.title: Atomic Blonde
movies.slug: Charlize Theron stars as an MI6 agent fighting through 1989 Berlin. Stylish, brutal action with Cold War intrigue.

sections.content: Salt marked a crucial evolution in how Hollywood portrayed female action heroes. Unlike earlier films that emphasized sexuality over capability, like La Femme Nikita (1990), Salt presented a protagonist whose gender was incidental to her skills and mission. This paved the way for films like Mad Max: Fury Road (2015) and Wonder Woman (2017), where female leads drive the action without their gender being the focus of the narrative.
